column1: # RECIPE_MEMORY.tsv - append-only lesson memory of recipe compression-20261106 (RELOCATE_COMPRESSION): one row per lesson, appended in the same commit as the correction.

column4: the develop head is the newest complete lineage: the six crate targets' develop blobs equal the crate's sha256-pinned postimages, the retained-variants/pr14341 copies are exactly the crate's pinned preimages (pre-reuse sink) and the held-pr16346 copies equal develop; the byte kernels' develop blob is the m3-lz-native-fastpaths-20261031 postimage (9510f829bb44), newer than the m3-lz-compression-20261030 pin (230bc5de9604)
column5: git rev-parse develop:<path> vs hash-pinned-java/<crate>/<file>.txt; sha256 of the retained variants vs the crate manifest preimage column

column4: the census row lists six files but the encoders do not compile alone: both construct M3LzMatchCandidateIndex and call M3LzByteKernels.commonPrefix, so the closure (two owners + the index oracle and its wrapper) is ported as FILE rows; the decoder pair, JNI kernels and four-way index are OMIT rows

the bitmatrix v3 recipe refuses a test import of org.junit.jupiter.api and of com.sun.management (neither a java./javax./jdk. prefix nor a mapped package); declared EXTERNAL rows admit them, the probe's JDK module jdk.management is added to the test compile only (--add-modules jdk.management, --add-reads org.m3jdk.compression=jdk.management) so the product descriptor stays java.base only
column5: first run REFUSED at M3CompressionWorkspaceTest; second run files=10 changed=4; jar --describe-module: requires java.base mandated

column4: derivation from the bitmatrix recipe is itself scripted (exact-anchor edits that refuse unless each anchor matches once): docstring, recipe path, removal of the CMake registration block, path constant and writer; everything else byte-identical

the format oracle reaches the encoders through method handles by class name, so one driver replays donor and relocated classes; its report carries no class name and no timing (timing goes to stderr), so the two reports compare byte for byte

a strict decoder that never rejects proves nothing: two one-line spec mutants (LZ4 LAST_LITERALS 5 -> 4, Snappy MAX_COPY_LENGTH 64 -> 65, which wraps the COPY_2 length field) shadow the relocated class on the class path and must be refused
column5: mutant lz4_last_literals REFUSED (LZ4 match reaches the last 5 bytes); mutant snappy_copy_length REFUSED (Snappy decoded size differs)

column4: every JVM (Maven, surefire, java) gets -Djava.io.tmpdir on the scratch drive: the Windows default temp is on a forbidden drive; surefire takes it through -DargLine, Maven through MAVEN_OPTS, the native lz4-java / snappy-java loaders of the scratch differential extract their libraries there
